title: Single release: Wonderful Christmastime by Paul McCartney | 1979
content:
Paul McCartney’s single ‘Wonderful Christmastime’ was released on 16 November 1979.

Written on a “boiling hot day in July”, ‘Wonderful Christmastime’ was based upon a synthesizer riff played on a Sequential Circuits Yamaha CS-80, and recorded solo during the sessions for the McCartney II album. It was McCartney’s first Christmas composition since The Beatles’ fan club messages in the 1960s.

A video for the song was filmed at the Fountain Inn in Ashurst, West Sussex on 16 November 1979. It was directed by Russell Mulcahy and featured the members of Wings, even though they did not feature on the recording.

In the UK, the single peaked at number six in the charts on 5 January 1980. In the United States it fared poorly, reaching number 83 on the Cash Box chart on 12 January, and did not enter the Billboard Hot 100 until December 2018.

The b-side was ‘Rudolph The Red Nose Reggae’, a novelty version of the Christmas classic which McCartney had recorded in 1975.
